Considera abastecerte de objetos curativos antes de dirigirte a tu siguiente combate.{pp}También se han añadido varias órdenes nuevas a la pantalla de grupo. Ahora puedes DESPEDIR a las unidades que ya no necesites en tu grupo. Una vez despedida, una unidad DESAPARECE PARA SIEPMRE, así que piénsalo bien antes de tomar una decisión.{pp}También puedes seleccionar CAMBIAR DE CLASE para cambiar una unidad a otra clase. Necesitarás una MARCA DE CLASE correspondiente a la clase deseada.{pp}Por último, puedes consultar las ARTES SUPREMAS de tus unidades. Para ejecutarlos, necesitas alcanzar ciertos rangos de habilidad con las armas. Consulta la GUÍA DE JUEGO del Informe Warren para obtener más detalles.

Un walister originario de Golyat. Su padre, Prancet, fue capturado por los Caballeros Oscuros cuando atacaron Golyat un año antes. {hero} se unió a la causa de la Resistencia walister y hostigó a los enemigos de su pueblo junto con su hermana Catiua y su amigo Vyce.

  Su pueblo lo llamó el Héroe de Golyat y pronto se convirtió en una figura destacada de la Resistencia.

He is currently in hiding with his sister Catiua, awaiting an opportunity to overthrow the Duke.

Miembro de la Resistencia walister y originario de Golyat. Se unió a la Resistencia tras liberar al duque Ronwey de su cautiverio en el castillo de Almorica, pero se alejó durante un tiempo debido a la participación de la Resistencia en la masacre de Balmamusa.
  Se ocultó junto a su hermana Catiua, pero finalmente regresó a la Resistencia cuando Sir Leonar le pidió ayuda tras la invasión bakram de Rhime. Ahora sigue combatiendo a los bakram para expulsarlos de las tierras walister.

texto_ingles:
{span 1f 744a 17 10 183230303130}  A Walister hailing from Golyat who leads the Order of {order}. He joined the Resistance after freeing Duke Ronwey from his imprisonment at Almorica Castle. Due to the massacre at Balmamusa he broke his ties with the Resistance and went into hiding with Catiua.
  In battle with Sir Leonar he learned the Duke planned to forge a secret treaty with the Dark Knights Loslorien. He set off for Rhime to stop the proceedings, but before he could act the duke was killed through Vyce's treachery. With the Resistance rudderless he offered to take the helm, and he now commands all of southern Valeria.

Con la Resistencia sin liderazgo, se ofreció a tomar el mando y ahora comanda todas las fuerzas del sur de Valeria.

texto_ingles:
{span 21 c64b 26 10 1c4830303130}  A Bakram hailing from Golyat who leads the Order of {order}. He joined the Resistance after freeing Duke Ronwey from his imprisonment at Almorica Castle, and later took part in the massacre at Balmamusa. Despite setbacks he eventually came to lead the Resistance against the Bakram and Dark Knight forces.
  He was reunited with his father, Prancet, at Brigantys Castle, and from him learned the truth of Catiua's past. Olivya also revealed he was actually born in Heim of Bakram descent, with his father the brother of Regent Brantyn Morne. He fulfilled his father's dying wish and led the Resistance to victory against the Dark Knights, defeating them in a bloody battle.

{span 1f f04a 27 18 0bc030313030 1ff030313030 0e9e30313130}  A Walister hailing from Golyat who grew up with {hero}. He was formerly the leader of the New Walister Alliance.
  Together with {hero} he rescued Duke Ronwey and joined the Walister Resistance. He later broke his ties with the Resistance after strongly opposing the massacre of innocent Walister at Balmamusa.   He eventually reconciled with the Resistance when {hero} took up its leadership. His might in arms served the Order of {order} well, helping bring the war to an end.

Un walister originario de Golyat que creció junto a {hero}. Antiguamente fue el líder de la Nueva Alianza walister.
  Junto con {hero}, rescató al duque Ronwey y se unió a la Resistencia walister. Después fundó la Nueva Alianza walister para defender el autogobierno de su pueblo y acabar con el dominio de la nobleza, ganándose el favor de muchos de los suyos.
  Finalmente se reconcilió con la Resistencia cuando {hero} asumió su liderazgo. Su destreza en combate sirve a la Orden de {order} en su esfuerzo por poner fin a la guerra.

{span 25 fa4c 10 18 115a30313030 25fa30313030 0cce30313030}  A Walister hailing from Golyat who grew up with {hero}. Together they rescued Duke Ronwey and joined the Walister Resistance, where he once commanded the Third Spear.
  He later took part in the massacre of innocent Walister at Balmamusa despite {hero}'s opposition, creating a rift between them. He continued to serve the Resistance thereafter, commanding a force reporting directly to the Duke. However, his lust for power led him to conspire with the Bakram and make an attempt on the lives of the Duke and the Dark Knight Lanselot. He was hanged by the Bakram after the plot failed.
  Following his death he was reanimated by the Necromancer Nybeth, but then defeated by {hero}, finally putting his tormented soul to rest.

texto_espanol_nuevo:
El verdadero nombre de Catiua era Versalia Oberyth. Era hija del Rey Dinasta y de Mannaflora, doncella de la reina. Poco después de nacer, Abuna Prancet la acogió y la crió en Golyat. No sabía nada de su linaje, salvo que Prancet no era su verdadero padre.
  Después de que el Caballero Oscuro Lanselot le revelara la verdad, Loslorien la obligó a acompañarlos con el pretexto de protegerla. Más tarde, las fuerzas de la Resistencia que avanzaban hacia el castillo de Barnicia la rescataron.
  Se puso del lado de la Resistencia con la esperanza de poner fin a la guerra y recuperar su trono, pero murió en combate antes de poder hacer realidad sus planes.

Xenobiano nacido en la ciudad de Valna, en Charlom, que antiguamente comandaba los Caballeros Sagrados del Reino de Nueva Xenobia. Llegó a Valeria por orden del rey Tristan de Xenobia para recuperar la espada Brynhildr.
  Estaba destinado en Rhime cuando los bakram invadieron la región. Aunque luchó con valor, fue superado en número y solo pudo escapar de Rhime gracias a la ayuda de {hero}. Después se unió a la Orden de {order} para ayudarles a poner fin a la guerra, pero más tarde murió en el campo de batalla.

Al igual que el Caballero Sagrado Lanselot, fue desterrado de Xenobia por mala conducta. texto_espanol_nuevo:
Xenobiano nacido en la ciudad dalmuhd de Konsh que antiguamente sirvió con los Caballeros Sagrados del Reino de Nueva Xenobia.
  Al igual que el Caballero Sagrado Lanselot, fue desterrado de Xenobia por mala conducta. Se unió a la Resistencia walister tras ayudar a {hero} a liberar al duque Ronwey de su cautiverio en el castillo de Almorica.
  Estaba destinado en Rhime cuando los bakram invadieron la región. Aunque luchó con valor, fue superado en número. Desde entonces no se ha vuelto a saber nada de él.

Bakram que lidera el Frente de Liberación.
  Antiguamente difundía las enseñanzas de la Orden de Philaha, cuyos miembros veneran al Gran Padre, pero la abandonó al perder la fe en la religión. Después fundó el Frente de Liberación con el objetivo de poner fin a la guerra mediante una revolución.

texto_ingles:
{span 21 424b 24 18 14bc30313030}  A Bakram who was once a sibyl of the Order of Philaha. She is the daughter of Archiereus Mreuva. After escaping political strife in Heim, she continued to pass on the teachings of the Order with her father. She joined the upper echelons of the Order upon her father's disappearance, and her stoutness of heart garnered much trust from the congregation.
  She came upon Abuna Prancet while traveling the Corpsevale on the outskirts of Heim, and took the ailing abuna to Brigantys Castle. When {hero} came to the castle she arranged for them to meet, and later told him of his lineage.
  She then joined the Resistance in the hopes that it would lead her to her own father.

texto_ingles:
{span 20 5649 27 18}  A Xenobian from Peshaval who once led the Beast Regiment of the Kingdom of New Xenobia.
  He is a close friend of Canopus. When Xenobia fell under the rule of the Sacred Xytegenian Empire, he bent to their will at first, reluctant to bring war upon his people.   After the Kingdom of New Xenobia was established, he traveled to the Holy Lodissian Empire.

texto_ingles:
{span 2c ac4c 05 18}  A Loslorien commander from Niemaran, a small town in the borderlands of Lodis. He is of Bolmoccan descent.
  He is last born of the former Nildahme royal house, which once wielded great power throughout the Sea of Lhai region. The Holy Lodissian Empire saw the bountiful lands of the Kingdom of Nildahme as ripe for the taking. They staged an uprising among the enslaved masses from which the ruling house had fattened their purse, then sent in their armies. Fearing for his life, the King hastily abandoned all resistance, and yielded to the Lodissians. Since then the Bolmoccans have endured lives of servitude.
  Andoras fled from a skirmish with Resistance forces while on a covert assignment.

Un comandante de Loslorien originario de Niemaran, una pequeña localidad de las tierras fronterizas de Lodis. Es de ascendencia bolmocana.
  Es el último descendiente de la antigua casa real de Nildahme, que antaño ejerció un gran poder en toda la región del mar de Lhai. El Sacro Imperio de Lodis vio las fértiles tierras del Reino de Nildahme como una presa fácil. Instigó una rebelión entre las masas esclavizadas, de las que la casa gobernante había obtenido grandes riquezas, y después envió sus ejércitos. Temiendo por su vida, el rey abandonó rápidamente toda resistencia y se sometió a los lodisianos. Desde entonces, los bolmocanos han vivido bajo la servidumbre.
  Andoras seguía resentido con Lodis por haber destruido su patria y se unió a Sir Martym y Sir Barbas en una rebelión contra el mando de los Caballeros Oscuros. Se apoderaron de Brynhildr y huyeron a los Jardines Colgantes.

The Holy Lodissian Empire saw the bountiful lands of the Kingdom of Nildahme as ripe for the taking. They staged an uprising among the enslaved masses from which the ruling house had fattened their purse, then sent in their armies. Fearing for his life, the King hastily abandoned all resistance and yielded to the Lodissians. Since then the Bolmoccans have endured lives of servitude.
  Andoras still harbored resentment toward Lodis for destroying his homeland, and he joined Sir Martym and Sir Barbas in revolt against the Dark Knight leadership. They took possession of Brynhildr and fled to the Hanging Gardens, but were slain there by the Resistance.

texto_ingles:
{span 15 044b 37 28 09ba30303130 140430313130}  A Walister hailing from the town of Sezhun in Almorica who serves in the Order of {order}.
  House Montrose is a noble family that has produced a great many knights over the years, and they are known for their loyalty to the duke. They live by the motto, "Serve with each sweep of the blade."
  When Leonar was made leader of the duke's personal troops, Voltare was appointed his second in command. His steadfast nature and closeness in age to Leonar forged a strong bond between them.
  Following the recapture of Almorica Castle, he met with ambush while pursuing the Necromancer Nybeth with Leonar. After {hero} came to their rescue, he left Leonar's side and became a member of the Order of {order}.

{span 14 9c4b 22 20}  High champion of the Dark Knights Loslorien.
  He was sent to Valeria when a secret treaty was forged between the Holy Lodissian Empire and the Bakram leader Brantyn. However, his true task was to occupy Valeria and seek the wondrous powers thought hidden there.

texto_ingles:
{span 2c 844b 07 10}  A Bakram who serves as regent to the Bakram-Valerian Kingdom. Following the death of King Dorgalua, he aspired to rule Valeria himself.
  Though once a mere abuna in the Order of Philaha, he used his growing power in the church to intervene in the power struggle caused by the lack of a successor. {span 27 2849 24 10 0c4430313030}  A Galgastani who served her clan in battle. Her surname, Canaletto, indicates she was of the people who inhabit the thickly forested region near the headwaters of the Theron river. {span 27 ca4d 1e 18 0a9e30313030}  A Bakram who is wed to the pirate Darza. She was born to nobility in Barnicia, but struck out on her own to escape the burden of her lineage. While at sea her ship was attacked by Darza's pirates, and she was taken to Ndamsa Fortress. She was unfazed by their threats of violence, and Darza grew fond of her spirited nature, keeping her always at his side. Veldrei eventually came to have feelings for Darza as well, and they married.
  At first she joined him on raids, but later stayed ashore to watch over their den after learning she carried Darza's child. Though usually calm and collected in front of the other pirates, she broke into tears upon hearing of Darza's death.
  She was defeated in battle by {hero} while attempting to avenge her husband's killing, but her life was spared.

{span 25 944b 0d 18 0a7c30313030}  A Galgastani who served his clan in battle. He was the son of renowned architect Selba Brondel. Selba created many famed buildings, such as Heilingham Palace, also known as the Hanging Gardens. Orba taught at the Coritanae Academy of Arts while painting numerous works in his spare time.   He encountered Resistance forces at Tynemouth while en route to Almorica, and was slain by {hero} Pavel.

{span 2f 184c 3c 18 0f7e30313030 0a7e30313030}  A Galgastani who served his clan in battle. He was the son of renowned architect Selba Brondel. His twin brother Orba was slain by {hero} at Tynemouth.
  Garba had won fame as a political philosopher, penning works such as "The Creed of the Self-Deceived" and "Failings of Present-Day Doctrine." Though initially an advocate of progressive politics, he took a more nationalistic tone after hearing the words of Hierophant Balbatos. He stated in one address, "Nothing can assuage the resentment we harbor toward the Walister, though we may know it unjust." The way he calmly vanquished his opponents in argument earned him the name "Garba the Silver-Tongued."

{span 1f e44d 2f 18 145430313030}  A Galgastani who led a band of pirates that plagued the Obero Sea. When Lontera was executed by the Valerian army, Darza took the helm in his stead.
  His wife Veldrei was born to nobility, but became a pirate after Darza raided the vessel on which she had taken passage near Boed Fortress. Veldrei stayed ashore to watch over their den at Ndamsa Fortress after learning she carried Darza's child.

texto_ingles:
{span 27 6e4e 0f 18 06d030313030}  A Galgastani who served his clan in battle. During the reign of King Dorgalua, deadly swordfights were a popular form of entertainment among wealthy Bakram in Heim. Only gladiators were permitted to participate in these bouts to the death. These gladiators were deserters or criminals chosen for their fighting ability. By choosing the path of the gladiator they escaped execution and were granted a small chance of freedom.
  Brezen was once a gladiator himself, surviving numerous bouts to eventually win his liberty. His skill in battle saw him recruited into the army, but he was disliked by others for his vulgar manners. He was bullied mercilessly and made the target of much unjustified scorn. Perhaps because of this, his prowess on the field of battle waned.
  He was killed after clashing with {hero} Pavel on the Golborza Plain.

texto_ingles:
{span 25 244c 30 18 0c7830313030}  A Walister who once served with the Walister Resistance. She was a spiritualist at the village of Vanan near the border of Almorica, contacting the dead to pass on messages to their kin. Regardless of whether her talents were genuine, Ramidos brought peace to many grieving loved ones. Her father died at an early age, and it is clear that her mother instilled in her a strong sense of compassion.
  She lived in Vanan with her son's family, but all her kin were slain when the village was sacked in the early days of the war. She then joined the Walister Resistance as a spellbinder, specializing in offensive magic.
  She was killed in battle when {hero} arrived at Almorica Castle to free Catiua, who had been kidnapped by Xapan the Mercenary.

{span 23 464b 22 18 06d230313030}  A Galgastani who served her clan in battle. House Apollinaire is a noble family related to former Lord of Coritanae, Count Orlandeau. For generations they have held seats in the House of Nobles, wielding great power throughout the region. Daesi Apollinaire, youngest daughter of the current family head, favored warfare over politics, eventually attaining the rank of commander.
  Galgastani commanders are charged with leading several legions of men, and are second in rank only to high commanders. Daesi was well suited to the role, demonstrating decisive leadership and superlative combat skills.
  She died attempting to fend off {hero}'s assault on Coritanae Keep.

  She was a necromancer who tampered with the souls of the dead. She studied under the Necromancer Nybeth together with her daughters Moldova and Cressida. They believed that necromancy allowed those who died before their time a chance to fulfill their ambitions.

  She started life as a pumpkin, but took on human qualities through her strong desire to be treated fairly.   In her spare time she busies herself growing pumpkins and perfecting her recipe for pumpkin pie.

{span 1a c64d 37 50}  The game records your last 50 actions during battle. You can use the Chariot Tarot to call up this battle record and return to a previous point in a fight. When jumping to a previous point it is saved as a separate record, so you can compare results from before and after you retraced your steps.

- Using the Chariot Tarot -
  Press the {icon 9} button during the attack turn of one of your units or after interrupting the turns of others. You can also select Chariot Tarot from the System Menu.

- Same Actions, Same Results -
  If you perform the same actions after retracing your steps using the Chariot Tarot, the results will also be the same. You must perform different actions to change your fate in battle.

- Battle Log -
  Press the {icon 4} button while the Chariot Tarot is displayed to view a detailed log of each turn.

{span 1e 8453 28 68}  You can use the World Tarot to jump to certain points in previously completed areas of the story. These are called "anchor points."

- Moving Between Anchor Points -
  There are multiple anchor points in each chapter. You can view these by using the World Tarot command in the Warren Report. This time line is also used to select a specific anchor point to jump to.

- The Story is Reset -
  Your progress is saved as you pass each anchor point. When you jump to an anchor point, you resume playing from that point in the story. If you return to a point before an important decision is made, you can make that decision again.

- Your Party Remains Unchanged -
  Party details such as class levels, inventory, and war funds are retained when you jump to an anchor point. This is also true of units added to your party, though they may revert to guests not under your control depending on story developments. Even in these cases, they will always return to your party once their duties are complete.

- Lost Information -
  Each anchor point records your progress up to the point at which you passed it. For this reason, anything occurring after the selected anchor point will be lost.

texto_ingles:
{span 1a d84e 11 30}  Each anchor point records your progress up to the point you passed it. The status of each unit relating to the story is also saved. This means that when you use the World Tarot, you may experience some inconsistencies.

  For example, assume you had dismissed Canopus before passing Anchor Point B. If you later jump to Anchor Point B using the World Tarot, even if Canopus happens to be in your party, the story will continue on as if he had been dismissed. The same is true of the information in the Warren Report.

- Updating Anchor Point Data -
  Each time you pass an anchor point the data it contains is updated. Using the example above, if you jump to an anchor point before Canopus was dismissed, then pass Anchor Point B again without dismissing him, the Anchor Point B data will be updated to reflect his presence in your party.

{span 18 0e4d 0c 50}  You can move between various locations and customize your party on the world map.

- Main Menu -
  Press the {icon 3} button while the cursor is on your party to display the Main Menu for the world map. The Party and Warren Report commands can be used at any point on the map, while the Shop command only appears when your party is at a town or castle.

- Traversing the Map -
  To move to locations such as towns and castles, position the cursor over the desired destination and press the {icon 3} button. Events or battles may be triggered when you arrive at or pass through a map location.

- System Menu -
  Press the {icon 12} button to display the System Menu. Select the Data command to save your progress to the storage media, and the Options command to change settings such as the controls.

texto_ingles:
{span 1c 3a57 23 78}  During battle the RT (Recovery Time) of units is compared to determine attack turn order, with units having lower RT taking their turn sooner. RT is determined by the base value for the unit, the weight of the equipment they carry, their class, and the actions they performed on their previous attack turn.

- Equipment Weight -
  Each piece of equipment displays a value for its weight. The greater its weight, the more it adds to the RT of units equipping it. It pays to take this into account when deciding which equipment to use.

- Class -
  Each class has a base RT value. The RT of similar units will vary depending on their class, affecting the order in which they act.

- Previous Attack Turn -
  Each action that is taken during an attack turn will have an impact on the RT for the next turn. This is determined by the distance covered with the Move command and the actions taken with Act and Skills commands. Equipment and spells also have RT values that are added to RT when they are used.

- Attack Turn List -
  When a unit is selected during battle, the row of units shown at the bottom of the screen indicates the expected AT order. To view the attack turn of all units in battle, press the {icon 4} button to display the Unit List, and use Sort Units to display them in order of attack turn.

  It is crucial to stay aware of which units will be acting next. Try to eliminate unnecessary actions to stay ahead of the enemy.

texto_ingles:
{span 16 404f 22 50}  Each unit has Life and HP that represent their physical endurance. Units whose HP falls to 0 during battle are incapacitated, and will lose a point of life if not aided. When a unit's life is exhausted, it is dead and can no longer be revived.

- Incapacitation -
  A counter appears above the heads of units incapacitated when their HP falls to 0. Each attack turn the counter decreases by 1, and if it reaches 0 that unit loses a life and is withdrawn from the battlefield.

- Withdrawn Units -
  Units withdrawn from the battlefield cannot take further actions during the current battle. However, they can take part in later battles as long as they have at least one point of life remaining.

- Death -
  Units that have no remaining life are deceased. Death is not reversible, so they will no longer be able to fight at your side. You can either Dismiss a deceased unit or Scavenge Skills to remove it from your party.

texto_ingles:
{span 14 804c 1f 40}  The movement range and elevation difference each unit can traverse vary depending on the movement type of its class. The skills assigned to a unit can also affect movement.
  The Move command can be reset and issued again up until the point another command is issued. This can be useful when you need to reposition a unit to be in range to attack.

- Crossing Gaps -
  Units can leap across gaps a single tile wide, but the other side of the gap must be of equal or lower elevation.

- Elevation Differences -
  The height a unit can jump up or down varies depending on its movement type. This can lead to situations where a unit can jump down to a lower spot but cannot climb back up, forcing a longer return route to be taken.

texto_ingles:
{span 18 5651 0d 80}  Magic-using classes such as Wizards must first make the following preparations to use spells:

- Learning Spells -
  To learn a spell you must first obtain the corresponding arcana. When you have an arcana in your possession, the spell contained within can be learned by selecting Magic under the Party command. Spells can also be learned by using arcana as items during battle.

- Command Skills -
  To use a spell you have learned, you must also learn the command skill for the spell's elemental school. Once a command skill has been learned, it must be assigned before it can be used in battle. After a skill is assigned, it will appear under the Act command.

Example: Casting Heal
1. Obtain the Grimoire Vitalite.

2. Select Learn under Magic from the Party screen, and then select Grimoire Vitalite. The unit will learn the Heal spell.

3. Select Learn under Skills from the Party screen, and learn the Divine Magic command skill.

4. Select Assign under Skills from the Party screen, and assign the Divine Magic command skill.

texto_ingles:
{span 18 7856 03 90}  Some of the more common debuffs include petrify, poison, stun, sleep, and charm.

- Petrify -
  Petrified units are turned to stone, leaving them powerless to act. Weapon attacks against them will always hit, but the damage done will be greatly reduced. The debuff can be removed using magic or items, and will also fade after a certain number of attack turns.

- Poison -
  Poisoned units will take damage for a set number of turns. The debuff can be removed using magic or items, and will also fade after a certain amount of RT has passed.

- Stun -
  Stunned units have a certain chance of losing the ability to act. The debuff can be removed using magic or items, and will also fade after a certain number of attack turns.

- Sleep -
  Sleeping units remain stationary and their avoidance of weapon-based attacks is reduced to 0%. The debuff can be removed using magic or items, and will also fade when the unit takes damage or after a certain number of attack turns.

- Charm -
  Charmed units are temporarily confused and attack their allies. The debuff can be removed using magic or items, and will also fade when the unit takes damage or after a certain number of attack turns.

  There are many other debuffs besides those listed here. When a unit is affected by a debuff, you can view details about it using the Condition command.

- Attack Types -
  The three attack types are CRUSHING, PIERCING, and SLASHING, and each has a corresponding resistance.

- Elements -
  The eight elements are AIR, EARTH, LIGHTNING, WATER, FIRE, ICE, LIGHT, and DARK, and each has a corresponding resistance.

- Races -
  The nine races are HUMAN, BEAST, REPTILE, DRAGON, DIVINE, UMBRA, FAERIE, PHANTOM, and GOLEM. Some races are more or less resistant to certain spells and weapons.

{span 12 c047 01 18}  Terrain information for the selected tile is displayed on the battlefield.

texto_ingles:
{span 1a b24f 26 50}  Experience points and skill points are calculated for the entire battle party and then distributed according to a number of rules.

- Experience Points -
  The experience point total is made up of the base value for the battle and the points added when enemy units are defeated. This number is then distributed based on the classes of the surviving party members. Classes with the greatest number of surviving units receive more experience points.

- Skill Points -
  Skill points are acquired through the actions taken by your units during battle, and then added to the battle party's skill point pool. The points in the pool are distributed evenly among surviving units once the battle is over.

- Zombies -
  Be wary if any of your surviving units are zombies. Units with this condition count towards the total for point distribution, but receive no actual experience or skill points, so their portion of the total is lost.

texto_ingles:
{span 1a 8653 02 88}  Skills are abilities that each unit can learn by spending the skill points they acquire. Each class has access to different skills, but some can be used by other classes once they have been learned. You can increase the number of skill slots by spending skill points, up to a maximum of 10 slots.

  The four skill types are command, support, action, and special.

- Command Skills -
  These add sub-commands that can be accessed using the Act command. Includes skills such as Divine Magic.

- Support Skills -
  Support skills take effect automatically once they are assigned. There are many kinds, such as those that change movement type or increase attack power.

- Action Skills -
  Action skills can be executed using the Skills command once they are assigned. They require TP to use.

- Special Skills -
  These include skills such as dragon breath that are only available to certain races. They appear under the Act command.

  Units can gain proficiency with certain skills when they are used in battle, raising their skill rank. You may even acquire finishing moves unique to certain weapons by raising the skill rank of your weapon skills.

texto_ingles:
{span 16 d451 36 48}  Sometimes an attack causes the target to be moved back one tile. This is called knockback. Knockbacks can occur due to critical hits, as well as skills and specific weapon attacks.
  There are certain situations in which knockback is impossible. In general, knockback moves the target back one tile, but this does not occur if the tile in question contains an obstacle or another unit, or if it is at a higher elevation than the starting tile.

- Causing Knockback -
  It is difficult to make critical hits consistently. Attacking with a shield is a more reliable method. Shields usually have a higher chance of causing knockback. There are also skills that raise the chance of successfully knocking a target back.

- Using Knockback -
  If an enemy is knocked down from a certain height, it will take additional damage from the fall. The damage increases with elevation and the weight of the unit.
  Knocking enemies into chasms or off walls can also cause that unit to lose a life and be removed from the battlefield. However, flying units are not affected by this.

texto_ingles:
{span 14 384c 15 48}  Support skills take effect automatically once they are assigned.

- Rampart Aura -
  This skill limits the movement of enemy units. A yellow line encircles tiles surrounding units with this skill assigned. Walking units entering this area are forced to stop regardless of whether they have movement left.

- Counterattack -
  This skill triggers a counterattack following an attack by an enemy unit. Units with this skill assigned will counterattack when targeted by a melee attack as long as their equipped weapon has the necessary range.

  There are many other support skills, such as those that change movement type or increase attack. Choose skills that complement a unit's class and the layout of the battlefield.

texto_ingles:
{span 10 5a4d 39 68}  You can sometimes befriend enemy units by using skills such as Recruit, Coax, and Subdue during battle. The chance of success is affected by range, loyalty, and HP.

- Range -
  You should try to get as close as possible to units you want to recruit. They will often ignore you if you merely shout at them from afar.

- Loyalty -
  Check the loyalty of the enemy unit. Units with lower loyalty are easier to recruit. You can judge the loyalty of a unit from the select help text when its name is selected.

- HP -
  Try to reduce the HP of the enemy unit as much as possible to increase your chances of success. One tenth their maximum HP is a good target.

- Failed Recruitment -
  Each time you fail at recruiting, the target's loyalty increases, making the next attempt more difficult. Try to make the first time count.

texto_ingles:
{span 14 084c 1a 50}  When battle ends, you will receive experience points, skill points, and the spoils of war. Units may also join or leave your party.

- Collecting Items -
  Bags of loot remaining on the battlefield are collected and the items inside added to your inventory. However, tarot cards are not recovered.

- Units Joining the Party -
  Enemy units you successfully recruit can be added to your party after the battle is over. If you already have the maximum number of units, you must either turn the new unit away or dismiss another unit first.

- Units Leaving the Party -
  If the loyalty of your units falls too low, they will leave after the battle is over. Take note if any of your units voice complaints at the end of a fight.

{span 28 e64a 36 10}  Valeria has a thriving sea trade, and many fortresses have been built to protect its ports from enemies. During King Dorgalua's reign soldiers of the Kingdom of Valeria were garrisoned at each fortress, but since the kingdom's downfall they have been manned sporadically at best. This has led to an increase in pirates, bandits, and army stragglers capturing the fortresses for their own use. Gecho Fortress on Beneceunga fell into pirate hands just the other day.
  As Gecho is south of the prominent trading port of Grimsby, merchants there are anxious to see the pirates routed from the fortress as soon as possible.

texto_ingles:
{span 15 fc4b 05 18 14fc30313030}  Though the war in Valeria is at an end, bands of armed militia still roam the lands. The Tigers of Burnham is one such group. Based in the Burnham Highlands, they have been implicated in a number of assassinations.
  They recently claimed that {hero} Pavel, leader of the Resistance, is using Princess Versalia to gain power for himself. They have stated their intention to capture Heim from the Resistance and restore rightful order under Versalia's rule.
  Though they fight under the banner of justice for all Valerians, former Bakram and Galgastani soldiers are joining their ranks in droves, and doubts have been cast on their motives.

texto_ingles:
{span 1a 8e4f 31 20}  The Bay of Gobanda is known for the thick fog that hangs over its waters. It was recently discovered that an immense tower lies hidden within the fog.
  Scholars from the Royal Academy say it once stood in the ancient city of San Bronsa, which was destroyed in Dorgalua's great war. The Bay of Gobanda was formed when magic wielded by King Rodrick of Brigantys shattered the lands in the last days of the war, also destroying San Bronsa.
  Scholars had studied the tower before the great war, but it is still not known when it was built, or by whom. It is said the Hanging Gardens built by King Dorgalua were inspired by the tower of San Bronsa.
  As news of the tower's discovery spreads there is concern it will be looted by thieves, and the Resistance is considering sending an exploratory party there. There have been further reports of a large island floating in the sky above the bay, but nothing more is known at this point.

texto_ingles:
{span 27 5a56 37 28 0d7630313030 265a30323030}  Many strange rumors have been circulating of late. People thought dead have been seen walking about, and the same person sighted in two places at once. Normally little stock would be put into such rumors, but there is much talk about these incidents among scholars and mages. Some believe them the work of the Apocrypha, others attribute them to some arcane art brought from Lodis.
  A common thread is found throughout these reports. The young hero of the Resistance, {hero}, is always mentioned by witnesses.
  {hero} is famed as a warrior and tactician, but few know of his penchant for collecting tarot cards. He is apparently particularly fond of the Wheel of Fortune card. It is not clear how this relates to the current rumors, but the Wheel of Fortune card has long been a symbol of regret and atonement in Valeria. It would not be beyond reason for {hero} himself to be struggling with such feelings, having experienced war at such a young age.
  What would one do if the power to bend time fell into our hands? One could repeat an exercise, knowing the best solution in advance. Or learn a lover plans to leave you before they speak a word. And who would not go back to save the lives of fallen comrades?
  However, one thing must be kept in mind: A different past is no guarantee of a happier future. Changing what has happened may in fact have no effect at all on the here and the now.

texto_ingles:
{span 20 8a54 06 20}  In times long past, mankind was engaged in a bitter battle with the forces of evil for supremacy over the land. Man drew strength from their gods, while the forces of evil suckled at the power of the Abyss. In the end, the people could do nothing against the overwhelming might of evil, and were pushed to the brink of destruction.
  It was at this time a group of three knights and twelve sages descended from the heavens and sealed the Chaos Gate that linked our world with the Abyss. The tide was turned, and man emerged victorious. Thus man came to rule and build the civilizations that stand today.
  The battle won, the three knights returned to the heavens, while the twelve sages remained to spread knowledge among the people. However, a burden yet weighed on their hearts. When the forces of evil fled, they foretold another Ogre Battle would occur. One of the knights bestowed a sword upon man that would grant the power to call the gods once more.
  The sword's name was Brynhildr. It is said he who wields the blade can speak with the gods, and travel to the heavens and the Abyss. The sword became an object of worship, and was hidden away until a second Ogre Battle saw need of its powers.

texto_ingles:
{span 14 864d 37 20}  On the island of Oedlark off the southernmost tip of Valeria are a series of undersea caverns known as the Pirate's Graveyard. They are legendary among treasure hunters, said to hold untold riches in their depths.
  The caverns are known for one other thing: countless pirates and thieves have sought to claim the treasures of the cavern as their own, but most lose their lives before even setting foot inside.
  Currents from the south and northwest converge in the waters surrounding the Pirate's Graveyard, and its reefs make navigation difficult for all but the most skilled sailors.
  Upon reaching the caverns explorers must contend with all manner of deadly creatures, and it is littered with the corpses of failed adventurers. It is no wonder that none have yet claimed the treasures said to lie within.

texto_ingles:
{span 18 f84c 16 18}  Many pirates and treasure hunters have lost their lives at the Pirate's Graveyard. Only one man has returned from its depths alive. The Dread Pirate Azelstan is known throughout the Obero Sea.
  Boasting superb navigation skills and uncommon prowess with the sword, he was a pirate among pirates. He was also known for his cruelty, said to have left a trail of blood wherever his ship sailed, and his name struck fear into the hearts of all.
  Soon after returning from the Pirate's Graveyard, Azelstan gave up pirating and disappeared. Many have speculated at why he retired in the years that have passed, some saying he was cursed by a spectre, others claiming his sword arm was maimed at the Pirate's Graveyard.

texto_ingles:
{span 1e 1c5e 1b 38}  The fifteen years of war before Valeria was unified is known as Dorgalua's great war.
  Before the unification, Valeria was divided into the five kingdoms of Barnicia, Phidoch, Almorica, Coritanae, and Brigantys. Each sought to expand their territory, and relations were volatile to say the least.
  The great war began after Lord Clemont of Barnicia was assassinated by armed militia seeking to usurp his leadership. The delicate balance of power soon crumbled, with Phidoch gathering its military might and declaring war on Barnicia and Almorica, while Coritanae joined the fray as Almorica's ally.
  The war stretched on for eight years, with Phidoch eventually occupying Barnicia and Almorica and installing governments there. Phidoch ruler King Ramonica was a Bakram, and he began suppressing the Walister, causing friction between the peoples that continues to this day. Great numbers of partisans struggled against him.
  Phidoch attacked Coritanae, and when formerly neutral Brigantys joined the war at the behest of Coritanae, the war spread throughout the entire Valerian Isles. Fighting soon reached a stalemate, but Brigantys began secretly supporting partisan groups, who then formed a rebel army in Barnicia.
  Coritanae ruler Count Orlandeau was killed in battle, and Coritanae fell under the rule of Brigantys. The rebel army of Barnicia then turned on Phidoch. Future king Dorgalua was leader of this rebel army. Beset on both flanks by Brigantys and the rebels, Phidoch fell at last, bringing the conflict to an end.   
  King Rodrick of Brigantys agreed to a truce with Dorgalua, but the conditions favored one side greatly, and it was broken within a month. Fighting began anew. The battle between Rodrick and Dorgalua continued for another year, with Dorgalua ultimately winning victory. Valeria was united under a single ruler at last.

{span 1a b448 16 10}  Towards the end of Dorgalua's great war, King Rodrick of Brigantys wielded terrible magic to break the deadlocked armies. The great power this unleashed defeated his enemies on the battlefield en masse, but slew his allies in kind. The surrounding lands were also shattered beyond recognition.
  Upon his victory over King Rodrick, King Dorgalua forbade the use of the Apocrypha, and hid them away. Knowledge of its very existence was lost to the sands of time.

texto_ingles:
{span 24 a64f 2a 20}  It is not commonly known that the Brigania Flats were once a lush paradise. The Bay of Gobanda was also once an inland area.
  In the final days of Dorgalua's great war, the lands were shattered by a man named Rodrick Desmoria, who was once King of Brigantys.
  He fought alongside King Dorgalua to unite Valeria, but in the end became his mortal enemy. He is known for using forbidden magic to wipe out those who opposed him. Though his reputation is marred by this, King Rodrick was an austere ruler who would not stand for injustice or compromise. He at first resolved to use the Apocrypha to aid his people, but it was this act that caused them to turn against him.
  It is said he died in captivity at Brigantys Castle after his defeat at the hands of King Dorgalua. Until his death he muttered constantly of the injustice he had suffered, and some say his spirit was called to the Palace of the Dead after his passing.

texto_ingles:
{span 26 4456 3f 28}  The war is at an end, and peace has returned to Valeria. Reconstruction work is moving at a swift pace across the lands, and although trade has not reached its previous levels, it recovers day by day. The markets once again throng with people, and fresh vegetables and fruit from far away countries line the stalls. The lively seafaring country of Valeria is back to its old self.
  Yet many still bear the wounds of war. Veterans of the fighting are left scarred, dealing with lost limbs, blindness, and paralysis.
  Princess Versalia has ordered these soldiers be granted a benefit through the Order of Philaha. This may cost up to a quarter of the kingdom's budget, and could climb to almost half if compensation for civilians is also approved.
  Those dealing with postwar matters such as these are at a loss to help those suffering trauma from the horrors they faced in the war. In many cases this trauma affects the everyday lives of victims, causing insomnia and anxiety, and it can only be alleviated through medicinal means. Sufferers sometimes turn to drink as a way of escape, and it is clear this is a problem than cannot be resolved through medical care alone.
  Archiereus Mreuva Phoraena heads a committee dealing with the postwar recovery that pledges support to all, regardless of background, class, or profession. Those seeking help should inquire at the nearest abbey.

texto_ingles:
{span 2b ba67 3f 40 10cc30313030}  The motives behind many of Loslorien's activities have long been a mystery; the attack on Golyat, a town on the island of Galdochae, chief among them. According to a statement made to the Bakram by Dark Knight commander Balxephon V. Rahms, they planned the attack after learning a group of rebels conducting raids on Heim was hiding there. However, this information was later revealed to be false, and Lodis paid reparation to Golyat for the damage done during the attack.
  Now their true intentions have been revealed. Loslorien conducted the raid without Bakram help, and not one but several commanders were present. The Dark Knight Balxephon was among them, and some witnesses say they saw High Champion Tartaros as well. Even if armed militia were taking refuge there, it is questionable that so many Loslorien elite would take part.
  Despite the many victims of the tragedy at Golyat, there was no record of rebels being captured. Though attempts were made to obtain such records after the war, documents listing the names of suspected rebels were never uncovered. This can mean but one thing: the Dark Knights knew from the start that no rebels were harbored there.
  So why would they commit so brutal an act? Loslorien attacked Golyat after learning of the existence of a daughter born to King Dorgalua, most likely through Regent Brantyn Morne. It is also thought they had no intention of forming a long-term alliance with Brantyn and the Bakram. They acted under the pretense of eliminating rebel forces to conceal their true intentions.
  Yet after all their efforts, they were not able to locate the Princess in the attack. Instead, they instilled a hatred of Lodis in the Walister and created the Hero of Golyat, {hero} Pavel.
  Two years have passed since the raid on Golyat. With the war at an end, and Loslorien now back in Lodis, peace has returned to Valeria. Golyat has recovered swiftly, and few traces of the war remain. It should not be long before Golyat regains its status as Oberon's Pearl.
  In the coming days the unveiling of a monument will take place in the central plaza in Golyat. The monument was constructed at the behest of Princess Versalia to honor the memory of those who died in the attack, and remember how those precious lives brought the people of Valeria together.
  The Valerian Isles are now host to many visitors. We can but hope that those who see this new symbol of Golyat will take home with them a desire for peace.
